parsed.explanation: Federal binary passport and entry-screening rules, a ban on congruent use of government single-sex facilities, and documented severe custody harms create tier-1 universal exposure that state protections cannot cancel. The state layer provides operative anti-discrimination, hate-crime and court recourse, and no execution or routine imprisonment for trans presence is documented. For a minor, state bans on gender-affirming care are an additional documented exposure. Combined regime is therefore elevated-risk: serious if outed at federal checkpoints/facilities, materially mitigated in state public accommodations.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order defines sex as binary at birth, stops X-marker and mismatched-marker passport processing, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025. Entry cable: document discrepancy or doubt about sex leads to refusal and extra evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility, not automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration for nationals; passport policy is challenged in court and some orders are blocked/enjoined. Status for foreign X documents is uncertain.
entry_documents.interaction: State driver's licence X marker since 2020 does not control federal passports or entry screening; a discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal or fraud consideration regardless of state protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No traveller-facing custody placement protocol, consular access detail, or remedy for custody abuse is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention for an immigration or document issue, not trans presence alone, exposes traveller to birth-sex/conversion-therapy custody practices; state civil-rights law does not govern federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. Parent map shows many states with government-building bans; this division's own bathroom-ban status is not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations since 2018, extended 2020; 88% poll support for protections in 2022. No documented state facility access congruent with identity is stated.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodations protection operates in state/private settings but does not cancel federal facilities ban or federal document screening at checkpoints and in federal buildings.

care_services.exposure: Adult care denial not documented for this division. Federal orders and proposed rules target care for minors, funding, and providers; several orders blocked/enjoined, status unresolved.
care_services.protection: State public-insurance transition-surgery ban lifted 2017; state anti-discrimination extended to health care 2020. No operative adult visitor care guarantee is documented.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor may access state-protected health care, but federal funding/rules and provider chilling can interact; for minors, see minors_guardians.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders remove gender-identity policy, ban trans athletes entering for women's sports, direct investigation/prosecution over school gender ideology, and counterterrorism documents use 'radical gender ideology'/'radically pro-transgender' framing. Eight-plus governments issued advisories by Mar-Apr 2025.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state hate-crime enhancements effective 2019 and gay/trans panic defence abolished 2024. Employment discrimination prohibited under 2020 Supreme Court ruling.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State protections and courts can remedy state-level discrimination, but federal threat-framing and enforcement discretion at borders, schools and federal agencies remain operative and are not pre-empted by state law.

minors_guardians.exposure: State laws: July 2024 banned gender-affirming medicine for minors and surgery from Jan 2025; Aug 2025 laws effective Jan 2026 ban puberty blockers, hormones and chest surgery under 18, with discipline for providers and a right to sue. Grandfather clause for treatment under way at Jan 2026. Sports ban for grades 5-12, stay status unresolved.
minors_guardians.protection: State highest court ruled 3-1 in Aug 2024 to protect trans students on privacy/autonomy; a fourth broader discrimination bill was vetoed. No visitor care exception is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor cannot obtain banned care in this state even if medically judged necessary; a parent/guardian faces provider-discipline chilling and possible federal investigation of schools facilitating social transition, though several federal orders are enjoined.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2025 census recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents, second-highest raw count, but no per-capita denominator, so no rate is established. Federal bathroom-capital arrest example is from another state, not this division. School and public hostility signals exist at federal level.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 17 July 2026 county court found a man violated state civil-rights act by striking a trans woman, showing state court enforcement for trans victim. Hate-crime enhancements and anti-bullying law cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State police/courts are documented responding to anti-trans assault, mitigating street risk in state jurisdiction; federal hostility and advisories do not negate that state-level recourse, nor does it cancel federal exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders are unresolved; practical exposure depends on measures in effect at travel. Multiple 'Do Not Travel' flags nationally and degrading 2026 legislation are documented, but not specifically for this division.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs, legal-aid FAQ, state court remedy in 2026 assault case, and some federal orders blocked/enjoined show functioning recourse, not guaranteed outcomes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work unevenly across sovereigns: state anti-discrimination relief is documented, federal passport/facility relief is litigated and uncertain, and custody abuse has no documented working remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-B in severity of routine detention: this case has no documented routine police stops, confiscation and fines for mere trans presence, and state courts have enforced trans protections. Higher risk than 0.35-B only in federal document/facility/custody exposures, which are more institutionalised.

Similar to 0.55-B: extended secondary screening for document discrepancy, discretionary refusal of entry, administrative rather than routine criminal penalties, and slow/uncertain appeals. This case is somewhat lower because federal facility ban and custody harms are harsher, and minor-care bans add exposure absent in the anchor.

Lower than 0.75-D: that anchor has equality protection for facilities, brief detention ending in release, and prosecution of attackers. Here federal binary documents, facility exclusion, potential permanent fraud finding, and documented custody abuse are tier-1 exposures not present there, despite comparable state anti-discrimination and court enforcement.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: state law protects a visitor in housing, employment, public accommodations and after assault, with a 2026 court remedy, but federal law governs the journey's sharpest points - passport sex, entry screening, federal facilities and federal custody - where binary rules, refusal/fraud risk, facility exclusion and documented conversion-therapy and abuse practices apply. State protections do not pre-empt those federal exposures. For minors, state care bans are a direct additional bar. No routine imprisonment or execution for trans presence is documented, so risk is elevated, not severe.
